Objective.Description: Clearly state the learning objective or goal for the lesson.
Examples: Students will understand the basics of algorithms.
Students will learn how to use a sensor in a simple circuit.

Grade Level.Description: Specify the appropriate grade level(s) for the lesson.
Examples: Grade 5
Middle School

Duration.Description: Indicate the total duration for the lesson in minutes.
Examples: 60 minutes
90 minutes

Materials Needed.Description: List all materials required for the lesson in bullet points.
Examples: Markers
Chart paper
Computers/Tablets
Specific software/tools

Key Vocabulary.Description: List key vocabulary words that students need to know for the lesson in bullet points.
Examples: Algorithm
Sensor
Environmental protection

Preparation.Description: List all preparation steps required before the lesson begins in bullet points.
Examples: Set up computers with necessary software
Prepare handouts and materials
Arrange the classroom for group work

Description: Introduce the topic and objectives of the lesson.
Discuss the importance of the lesson's subject matter.
Investigate initial questions or ideas to spark interest.
Examples: Show a video or presentation related to the topic.
Ask probing questions to initiate discussion.
Perform a quick demonstration or experiment.

Description: Allow students to explore the topic through hands-on activities or research.

Examples.What to build: Create a simple circuit with a motor.
Examples.What to brainstorm: Programming ideas for running a motor using a sensor.

Description: Share progress and demonstrate models or findings.
Facilitate sharing and inspiration from peers.
Examples: Students present their initial models or research findings.
Class discusses the different approaches and solutions.

Description: Continue sharing and brainstorming from Part A.
Examples: Repeat sharing and discussing new ideas or refinements.

Description: Continue building and programming models or working on projects.
Share completed models and explain their functions.
Examples: Students finalize their projects and present them to the class.
Class discusses the learning outcomes and real-world applications.

Description: Use guiding questions to assess student understanding and decision-making.
Observe and record student progress using a checklist or rubric.
Examples: Teacher asks specific questions to gauge student comprehension.
Teacher uses a checklist to track student progress and participation.

Self-Assessment.Description: Provide a method for students to reflect on their own learning.
Examples: Blue brick: Follow instructions to create a program.
Yellow brick: Follow instructions to create a program.
Green brick: Follow instructions to create a program and help a friend.

Peer Feedback.Description: Encourage positive feedback and constructive suggestions within small groups.
Examples: Students provide feedback to each other on their projects.
Class discusses the importance of constructive criticism.

Differentiation.Description: Adapt the lesson to meet the needs of diverse learners.
Examples: Simplify: Limit research to a few community actions.
Increase Difficulty: Programs respond to user input or add a second response.

Extension.Description: Suggest additional activities or projects to extend learning.
Examples: Research another community action for environmental protection and present findings.

Standards.Description: Align the lesson with relevant educational standards.
Examples: Language Arts: CCSS.ELA-LITERACY.W.5.7

Specific Instructions to Highlight: Emphasize critical steps and instructions that should not be overlooked.
Enhancing Results: Tips on how to achieve better learning outcomes.
Areas of Caution: Highlight potential challenges or common pitfalls to avoid.
Engagement Strategies: Techniques to keep students engaged and motivated throughout the lesson.
